title: Find the first index of a character
description:
Write a function `first_index(text, char)` that returns the position of the first occurrence of `char` in `text`.

Covers source items 20-21 (first index of 'C', first index of 'F') as one exercise.
hints: text.index(char) scans from the start and returns the position of the first match - unlike .find(), it raises an error if char isn't present at all, which is fine here since every test case is guaranteed to match.
Call .index() on text with char and return the result.
expected_behavior: Returns the index of the first occurrence of char.
explanation: str.index() and str.find() both search forward from the start, but index() raises ValueError on no match while find() returns -1 - index() is the right choice when the caller already knows the character is present.
